questions.prompt: What is the special property of carbon that lets it form chains and rings, giving millions of organic compounds?
questions.explanation: Catenation is carbon's ability to bond to other carbon atoms, forming long chains and rings.

questions.prompt: How many covalent bonds does a single carbon atom usually form?
questions.explanation: Carbon has 4 valence electrons, so it forms 4 covalent bonds.

questions.prompt: What is the molecular formula of the alkene that contains 3 carbon atoms?
questions.explanation: Alkene formula is CnH2n; with n = 3, H = 2x3 = 6, giving C3H6 (propene).

questions.prompt: Two members next to each other in a homologous series differ by which unit?
questions.explanation: Each member of a homologous series differs from the next by a -CH2- group.

questions.prompt: A hydrocarbon has the molecular formula C5H8. To which family does it belong?
questions.explanation: CnH2n-2 with n = 5 gives C5H8, the general formula of an alkyne (one triple bond).

questions.prompt: Complete combustion of one molecule of methane (CH4) produces how many molecules of water?
questions.explanation: CH4 + 2O2 -> CO2 + 2H2O, so two water molecules are produced per molecule of methane.

questions.prompt: An oxide is a compound of an element combined with which other element?
questions.explanation: An oxide is any compound formed between an element and oxygen.

questions.prompt: A water-soluble base is given the special name:
questions.explanation: A base that dissolves in water is called an alkali; all alkalis are bases but not all bases are alkalis.

questions.prompt: Which oxide is amphoteric, reacting with both acids and bases?
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide (Al2O3) is amphoteric; Na2O and CaO are basic while CO2 is acidic.

questions.prompt: Which property is typical of a basic (alkaline) solution?
options: Reacts with metals to give hydrogen
questions.explanation: Bases turn red litmus blue, taste bitter, feel slippery and have pH greater than 7.

questions.prompt: When hydrochloric acid reacts with calcium hydroxide, what salt is formed?
questions.explanation: 2HCl + Ca(OH)2 -> CaCl2 + 2H2O; the chloride from the acid and calcium from the base give calcium chloride.

questions.prompt: A solution of pH 2 has a hydrogen-ion concentration how many times greater than a solution of pH 4?
questions.explanation: Each pH unit is a factor of 10; a difference of 2 units means 10 x 10 = 100 times more H+ ions.

questions.prompt: What does an electrolyte contain that allows it to conduct electricity when molten or dissolved?
questions.explanation: An electrolyte conducts because it contains free-moving ions that carry the electric charge.

questions.prompt: During the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, what is correctly formed at the anode?
questions.explanation: Chloride anions move to the anode and lose electrons (oxidation) to form chlorine gas; sodium forms at the cathode.

questions.prompt: According to OIL RIG, oxidation is the:
questions.explanation: OIL RIG: Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain of electrons.

questions.prompt: During the electrolysis of molten lead bromide, to which electrode do the Pb2+ ions move?
questions.explanation: Positive cations like Pb2+ move to the negatively charged cathode, where they are reduced.

questions.prompt: Which statement about a galvanic (voltaic) cell is correct?
options: It uses electricity to cause a reaction
The anode is the negative terminal
questions.explanation: In a galvanic cell a spontaneous reaction makes electricity; oxidation occurs at the anode, which is the negative terminal.

questions.prompt: In the electrolysis of acidified water, what is the ratio of the volume of hydrogen to oxygen gas collected?
questions.explanation: 2H2O -> 2H2 + O2, so twice the volume of hydrogen forms compared with oxygen, a 2 to 1 ratio.

questions.topic: Chemistry in Industry and Environmental Pollution
questions.prompt: Which raw material is mainly processed to produce sugar in Ethiopian sugar factories?
questions.explanation: Sugar is produced from sugar cane; cotton makes cloth, limestone makes cement, and hides make leather.

questions.topic: Chemistry in Industry and Environmental Pollution
questions.prompt: In the blast furnace reaction Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2, the carbon monoxide acts as the:
questions.explanation: CO removes oxygen from the iron oxide, so it is the reducing agent (it is itself oxidised to CO2).

questions.topic: Chemistry in Industry and Environmental Pollution
questions.prompt: A naturally occurring rock or mineral from which a metal can be extracted profitably is called a:
questions.explanation: An ore is a naturally occurring mineral that contains enough metal to be extracted profitably.

questions.topic: Chemistry in Industry and Environmental Pollution
questions.prompt: Sulphur dioxide released by burning fuels and factories is the main cause of which environmental problem?
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide (with oxides of nitrogen) dissolves in rain water to form acids, causing acid rain.

questions.topic: Chemistry in Industry and Environmental Pollution
questions.prompt: Iron is extracted from iron(III) oxide in a blast furnace mainly because carbon (or carbon monoxide) can:
options: Remove the oxygen from the ore
questions.explanation: Carbon is more reactive than iron toward oxygen, so it removes the oxygen (reduction): Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2.

questions.topic: Chemistry in Industry and Environmental Pollution
questions.prompt: Why can sodium NOT be extracted from its ore by heating with carbon?
options: Sodium is less reactive than carbon
Sodium is more reactive than carbon
Sodium does not form an oxide
questions.explanation: Sodium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot remove the oxygen; electrolysis of the molten compound is required.
